title: With a line's category row empty only that line's cost is held
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Make sure AccountingHub is enabled for the organization and the test location has no QuickBooks Online connection.
  • Have a new No Charge category for this test, category A, whose Account Mappings row is empty.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A.
  • Have a new work order for this test, work order 1, for customer A, in status Complete, billable, with line 1 billable and line 2 marked No Charge under category A with one stock part costing $40.00.
custom_steps:
1. Open work order 1.
  2. Click Create invoice.
  3. Open Accounting > Sales > Invoices.
  4. Open Accounting > Accounting Events.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Work order 1 opens.

Step 2:

  • The invoice is created.

Step 3:

  • The invoice, its revenue and its receivable are posted at once.

Step 4:

  • Only line 2's cost entry is Held, with the reason "No Charge: [category A's name] row not mapped".

Words in square brackets in a message stand for the value they name, such as the work order's number or the customer's name exactly as it is saved; every other word of the message must match exactly.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11765 (Story 8, AccountingHub, the closed work order and its parts cost)

  • S8-R7: “An invoice of a billable work order with no-charge lines (Story 12) reaches the hub as an ordinary invoice record with its revenue and receivable on the billable lines. The record carries a "No Charge lines" block: line number and title, category, original work order and line, original technician, hours, parts cost, expense account. The posting splits the parts cost: billable lines to the parts cost of goods sold account as today, each no-charge line to its category's mapping row (S6-R1). When a no-charge line's category row is empty, the invoice, its revenue and its receivable post at once and only that line's cost entries are held, with the reason "No Charge: [Category] row not mapped", until the row is mapped (S8-N2); a reversal that withdraws them marks them Dismissed (S4-R3). In Journal Entries the source of a no-charge line's entry reads "No Charge line".”
  • S8-N2: “If a mapped account on either side of the entry is missing or inactive, or the posting date falls in a closed fiscal period or in none, the event gets a status Held (new in the hub) on the Accounting Events page with the reason ("No Charge: [Category] row not mapped" or "Internal: [Category] row not mapped", the list name telling the two apart (S8-R7), "Shop supplies expense is not mapped", "Inventory asset is not mapped", "Parts cost of goods sold is not mapped", "Period [name] is closed", or the hub's existing "No open fiscal period covers [date]."), the existing Retry action, and automatic retry when the mapping is saved or the period opened. Other events for the organization keep flowing. A held Close withdrawn by Reopen becomes Dismissed (S4-E1). Held exists for these work-order entries only (Close, reversal, no-charge line, and the move of a vendor bill or credit line to its category account, S8-R3); invoices, vendor bills, credits and payments keep today's statuses.”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Hub event held | "No Charge: [Category] row not mapped" / "Shop supplies expense is not mapped" / "Period [name] is closed" | Reason on the Held event, Retry”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
